questions.enonce_markdown: Show that the length of arc $L$ of the curve $y = \cosh x$, for which $0 \le x \le a$ is $\sinh a$. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
For a curve $y = f(x)$ the arc length is $L = \displaystyle\int_0^a\sqrt{1 + \left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2}\,dx$.

Here $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \sinh x$, and $1 + \sinh^2 x = \cosh^2 x$. Since $\cosh x > 0$, $\sqrt{\cosh^2 x} = \cosh x$. Hence

$$L = \int_0^a\cosh x\,dx = \Big[\sinh x\Big]_0^a = \sinh a - \sinh 0 = \sinh a. \qquad \blacksquare$$

questions.enonce_markdown:
Further show that the area of the surface generated when the arc $L$ is rotated completely about the $x$-axis is

$$\frac{\pi}{2}\left(2a + \sinh 2a\right).$$ *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The area of the surface generated by rotating the arc about the $x$-axis is

$$S = 2\pi\int_0^a y\sqrt{1 + \left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2}\,dx = 2\pi\int_0^a\cosh x\cdot\cosh x\,dx = 2\pi\int_0^a\cosh^2 x\,dx,$$

using $\sqrt{1 + \sinh^2 x} = \cosh x$ from part (i).

Use $\cosh^2 x = \dfrac{1 + \cosh 2x}{2}$:

$$S = 2\pi\int_0^a\frac{1 + \cosh 2x}{2}\,dx = \pi\left[x + \frac{\sinh 2x}{2}\right]_0^a = \pi a + \frac{\pi}{2}\sinh 2a.$$

Factorising $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$:

$$S = \frac{\pi}{2}\left(2a + \sinh 2a\right). \qquad \blacksquare$$
